title: Base change of the orientation and of the tensor map
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X,Y,Y'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$, and let $v:Y'\to Y$ be any $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $u:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$ [def-pc-base-change].

Use either (i) a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$, with the ordinary constant-$A$ pro-etale module derived categories and bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories of [det-sp-finite-general-ring], or (ii) a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$, $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$, and the ordinary derived categories of varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] and their full uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. No normalization of an input tower is assumed. Write $B$ for $A$ or for the coefficient system $A_\bullet$, and $\mathcal C_T(B)$ for the corresponding constructible finite-Tor category. Pullbacks, tensor products, shifts and twists are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-tensor, def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with the finite-$A$ twists specified in [det-sp-finite-general-ring] and tower operations as in [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. All tensor products here are ordinary derived tensor products over $B$, not completed tensor products.

Let $F_f=Rf_{!,B}\dashv G_f=f_B^!$ be the constructible adjunction, and put $\omega_{f,B}=G_f B_Y$. At finite coefficients use [det-sp-finite-general-ring, def-pur-co-smoothness]; for towers use [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Let $\beta:v_B^*F_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}u_B^*$ be compact-support base change and define $e_K:u_B^*G_fK\to G_{f'}v_B^*K$ to be the adjoint transpose of
$$v_B^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ\beta_{G_fK}^{-1}:F_{f'}u_B^*G_fK\to v_B^*K.$$
At finite coefficients these are the canonical smooth exceptional exchanges of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness, def-exchange-projection]; for towers they are those of [det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc]. Identify $v_B^*B_Y=B_{Y'}$ and write $e_1:u_B^*\omega_{f,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f',B}$ for the unit component. Let $L_{f,B}=B_X(d)[2d]$ and $a_{f,B}:L_{f,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f,B}$ be the inverse of the diagonal orientation: [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object, det-sp-finite-general-ring] at finite coefficients and [det-sp-tower-gamma](1) for towers. Let $t_{f,K}:f_B^*K\otimes^L\omega_{f,B}\to G_fK$ be the transpose of inverse projection formula followed by $1_K\otimes\varepsilon_{f,1}$, as in [def-pur-co-smoothness, det-sp-finite-general-ring, det-sp-tower-gamma](2). Define $\gamma_{f,B}(K)$ by twist reassociation followed by $1\otimes a_{f,B}$ and $t_{f,K}$, as in [def-pur-smooth-purity-map, det-sp-finite-general-ring, det-sp-tower-gamma]. Then:

1. Under the canonical twist/pullback identification $u_B^*L_{f,B}=L_{f',B}$, one has $e_1\circ u_B^*a_{f,B}=a_{f',B}$.
2. For every $K\in\mathcal C_Y(B)$, under $u_B^*f_B^*=f_B'^*v_B^*$ and the monoidal pullback comparisons, one has
$$e_K\circ u_B^*t_{f,K}=t_{f',v_B^*K}\circ(1_{f_B'^*v_B^*K}\otimes e_1).$$

Consequently, with the same source identifications,
$$e_K\circ u_B^*\gamma_{f,B}(K)=\gamma_{f',B}(v_B^*K).$$

proof.text:
First take $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$, $r\geq1$. Write $W=X\times_YX$, $p_1,p_2:W\to X$ and $\Delta:X\to W$. In the analogous primed diagram, $W'$ with its projection $p_1'$ and section $\Delta'$ is the pullback of $(W,p_1,\Delta)$ along $u:X'\to X$: both fibre products represent pairs of points of $X$ over the same point of $Y$, together with a lift of that point to $Y'$. The identities $p_2\Delta=1$ and $p_2'\Delta'=1$ are preserved. Let $\kappa_f:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f,R}$ be the comparison in [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. Its pullback comparison is the one obtained from $e_1$ for $f$ and the exceptional comparison for $p_1$. Indeed [fix-lem-exchanges](2) says that compact-support exchanges respect horizontal and vertical pasting at these finite coefficients. The corresponding compact-support squares paste to the same square; applying [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1)-(2) to their inverse compact-support exchanges gives the same exceptional comparison, and the identity square has identity mate by clause (4). Thus the $C$-to-$\omega$ identification respects these specified, counit-defined exchanges, rather than an unspecified isomorphism. The smooth and pure-relative-dimension hypotheses for $p_1,p_1'$ follow from [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1). The diagonal is a closed section because $f$ is separated, as asserted in [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]. More explicitly, put $q:W'\to W$, let $b_f:p_2^*\omega_f\to\omega_{p_1}$ be the exceptional exchange in the diagonal square, and let $b_{p_1}:q^*\omega_{p_1}\to\omega_{p_1'}$ be the exchange along $u$. The two pasted-square expressions give
$$b_{p_1}\,q^*b_f=b_{f'}\,p_2'^*e_1.$$
Since $\kappa_f=\Delta^*b_f^{-1}$ and $p_2'\Delta'=1$, pulling this equation back along $\Delta'$ and rearranging gives
$$\kappa_{f'}\,\Delta'^*b_{p_1}=e_1\,u^*\kappa_f,$$
which is the required compatibility for the first arrow of the orientation construction. The witnessed finite pro-etale domain required by [fix-lem-exchanges] is available: [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] gives an etale constructible finite-Tor representative for each constructible finite-Tor object used here. Its scheme hypothesis holds because our separated finite-type $k$-schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated; its coefficient hypothesis holds because $R$ is finite and hence discrete Noetherian. Choose such witnesses before applying exchange pasting.

source.place: Orientation paragraph: base-changed diagonal and the specified exceptional exchange

proof.text:
For this smooth closed-section pair, let $N=N_{\Delta/W}$, with projection $\pi_N$ and zero section $z$, and let $\delta:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_N,z)$ be [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]. By [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](1),(5), the deformation family and its fibres commute with the arbitrary base change $u$; taking the fibre at $0$ identifies the primed normal-bundle pair with the pullback of $(N,z)$. The rank is $d$ by [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]. Write $b_N:\omega_{\pi_N}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_N(d)[2d]$ for vector-bundle purity. By [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity], $b_N$ commutes with base change and with the adjunction comparisons. The diagonal orientation is the composite
$$\Pi_{f,R}:\omega_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\kappa_f^{-1}}C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\delta}z^*\omega_{\pi_N}\xrightarrow{z^*b_N}R_X(d)[2d].$$
This spells out the canonical diagonal construction of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]; its chart normalization is exactly [det-sp-orientation-charts]. The first arrow respects the exchange by step 1, the second by the arbitrary-base-change assertion of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and the third by vector-bundle purity. Pullback of the displayed three-arrow composite is therefore its primed composite, so $\Pi_{f',R}e_{1,R}=u_R^*\Pi_{f,R}$. Taking inverses gives $e_{1,R}u_R^*a_{f,R}=a_{f',R}$. Here $u$ need not be flat: DNC base change is used only for a smooth morphism with a closed section, precisely the hypothesis of the cited geometry and invariance statements.

source.place: Orientation paragraph: deformation, normal bundle, vector-bundle integration, and coordinate normalization

proof.text:
Let $A$ be any finite commutative ring with $\ell^rA=0$, and write $(-)_A=-\otimes_R^LA$. By [det-sp-finite-general-ring](1)-(2), its diagonal orientation is characterized by $\Pi_{f,A}c_f=(\Pi_{f,R})_A$, where $c_f:(\omega_{f,R})_A\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f,A}$. The mixed exchange identity of [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport], applied to $f$ and $v$, is $e_{1,A}u_A^*c_f=c_{f'}(e_{1,R})_A$. Canonical pullback/tensor comparisons are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Hence
$$\Pi_{f',A}e_{1,A}u_A^*c_f=\Pi_{f',A}c_{f'}(e_{1,R})_A=(\Pi_{f',R}e_{1,R})_A=(u_R^*\Pi_{f,R})_A=(u_A^*\Pi_{f,A})(u_A^*c_f).$$
Cancel the isomorphism $u_A^*c_f$. Inverting the resulting equation proves clause (1) for $A$. This includes $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$: if $\ell$ is a unit times $\varpi_E^e$, this is $A_{E,en}$, with no unramifiedness assumption. Twist identifications here are the exponent-independent ones in [det-sp-finite-general-ring].

source.place: Orientation paragraph: the finite-level calculation with general finite coefficients

proof.text: For towers, [det-sp-tower-gamma](1) supplies actual orientation morphisms $a_f,a_{f'}$ in the ordinary tower derived categories, and [det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc](2) supplies an actual $e_1$ evaluating to the finite exceptional maps. Put $L=A_{\bullet,X'}(d)[2d]$ and $h=a_{f'}^{-1}e_1u_\bullet^*a_f\in\operatorname{End}(L)$. Step 3 says $h_n=1$ at every $n$. The twists before shifting are towers of sheaves by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed, sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Remove $[2d]$. Since $\operatorname{Tow}$ is abelian and evaluation is exact [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian](1)-(2), full faithfulness of the single-complex embedding [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies $h$ with a unique endomorphism of the sheaf tower $A_{\bullet,X'}(d)$. Its $n$th sheaf component is the identity by the same full faithfulness at finite level. Morphisms of towers are componentwise families [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], so this endomorphism is the identity. Consequently $h=1$ and $e_1u_\bullet^*a_f=a_{f'}$. This proves tower clause (1) without claiming faithfulness of evaluation on arbitrary derived morphisms.

source.place: Orientation paragraph: equality between shifted tower sheaves, tested at each level

proof.text:
We use the projection/base-change compatibility [lem-sp-compact-projection-base-change] for the compactification $f=pj$ and its pullback, in its setting (i) for finite $A$ and in its setting (ii) for towers. Its maps are the ones occurring in this proof. At finite coefficients its exchange $\beta$ and projection map are the compactification composites of [def-exchange-projection], formed with the constant ring $A$ in place of the residue ring (the same defining formulas with ordinary constant-$A$ ringed-module adjunctions; no residue-ring-only theorem is applied to $A$). For towers they are the levelwise-formed compactification projection and exchange maps of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2), and the exchange is $\beta_{f,\bullet}$ of [det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc](1). Write $q_f(K,M):F_f(f^*K\otimes M)\to K\otimes F_fM$ for the inverse projection formula, with tensor symmetry understood. Take $M=\omega_f$. The projection map of $f$ at $(\omega_f,K)$ is invertible by the finite tensor-map construction [det-sp-finite-general-ring](3) or the tower construction [det-sp-tower-gamma](2); the projection map of $f'$ at $(u^*\omega_f,v^*K)$ is invertible because it corresponds, by naturality in its first argument and the isomorphism $e_1:u^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$ of clause (1), to the projection map at $(\omega_{f'},v^*K)$, invertible by the same constructions for $f'$. The exchanges $\beta_{\omega_f}$ and $\beta_{f^*K\otimes\omega_f}$ are invertible by compact-support base change (finite coefficients) and [det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc](1) (towers; the objects lie in the constructible finite-Tor category by step 6 and [det-sp-tower-gamma](2)). The inverse form of [lem-sp-compact-projection-base-change] then gives
$$(v^*K\otimes\beta_{\omega_f})\,v^*q_f(K,\omega_f)\,\beta_{f^*K\otimes\omega_f}^{-1}=q_{f'}(v^*K,u^*\omega_f).$$
For towers this is an identity in the tower derived category itself, not inferred from equality of finite derived evaluations.

source.place: Tags 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); compactification composition and the explicit open-adjunction check above

proof.text: All transposes in the following calculation are on their stated constructible finite-Tor domains. For tower $K$ with common Tor interval $[a,b]$, pullback $v^*K$ has the same bounds by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] applied at $A_n=A_{E,en}$, since exact levelwise pullback preserves the cohomological interval. The same node supplies constructibility at each level; the definition [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers] therefore puts $v^*K$ in the uniform category. The source $f'^*v^*K\otimes\omega_{f'}$ belongs to it by [det-sp-tower-gamma](2), and $u^*(f^*K\otimes\omega_f)$ is isomorphic to this source by clause (1) and the monoidal comparison. Thus the tower adjunction [det-sp-tower-gluing] applies. For general finite $A$, use [sk-lem-sf-flat-model] to represent $K$ by a bounded complex $P$ of flat constructible $A_Y$-sheaves. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] says that $v^*P$ has flat terms and is K-flat. Exact constant-coefficient inverse image is the termwise computation of $Lv^*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so it preserves the finite degree interval of $P$. The terms of $v^*P$ are constructible: pull the finite stratification for each term back along $v$, intersect these finitely many partitions, and pull the locally constant finite local models back on each stratum, exactly the condition of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. For every sheaf $N$ in degree zero the tensor $v^*P\otimes N$ has terms only in that same finite interval, and hence zero cohomology outside it; the K-flat computation makes this the required derived tensor. Thus $v^*K$ has finite Tor amplitude. To check constructible cohomology as well, apply the same pulled-back stratification argument to the finitely many constructible cohomology sheaves of $K$; exactness gives $\mathcal H^i(v^*K)=v^*\mathcal H^i(K)$. This puts $v^*K$ in the finite category of [det-sp-finite-general-ring]. Its oriented tensor source is a twisted shift of its pullback, so is an allowed input for the stated adjunction and tensor map. No normalization of towers or flatness of the quotient $A_n\to A_m$ is used.

source.place: Tensor-map paragraph: domains of the finite and tower adjunctions

proof.text:
Write $F=F_f$, $F'=F_{f'}$, $G=G_f$, $G'=G_{f'}$, suppress the coefficient index, and put $P=f^*K\otimes\omega_f$, $K'=v^*K$. By the defining transpose of $e_K$ (finite: [def-pur-co-smoothness] for its unit component and [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] for the general counit mate; tower: [det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc](2)),
$$\varepsilon'_{K'}F'(e_K)=v^*\varepsilon_K\,\beta_{GK}^{-1}.$$
The tensor maps are the transposes of $(1\otimes\varepsilon_1)q_f(K,\omega_f)$ by [def-pur-co-smoothness, det-sp-finite-general-ring, det-sp-tower-gamma]. Using naturality of $\beta$, then this defining transpose, then step 5 gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon'_{K'}F'(e_Ku^*t_{f,K})
&=v^*\varepsilon_K\,\beta_{GK}^{-1}F'u^*t_{f,K}\\
&=v^*(\varepsilon_KF t_{f,K})\,\beta_P^{-1}\\
&=v^*((1\otimes\varepsilon_1)q_f(K,\omega_f))\,\beta_P^{-1}\\
&=(1\otimes(v^*\varepsilon_1\,\beta_{\omega_f}^{-1}))\,q_{f'}(K',u^*\omega_f)\\
&=(1\otimes(\varepsilon'_1F'e_1))\,q_{f'}(K',u^*\omega_f)\\
&=(1\otimes\varepsilon'_1)q_{f'}(K',\omega_{f'})F'(1\otimes e_1)\\
&=\varepsilon'_{K'}F'\bigl(t_{f',K'}(1\otimes e_1)\bigr).
\end{aligned}$$
The fifth line is the same counit identity at the unit; the sixth is naturality of projection formula in its second input. By injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection, the first and last maps have equal transposes and are equal. This proves clause (2) simultaneously at finite coefficients and in the tower derived category.

source.place: Tensor-map paragraph: counit calculation with the two transposes written explicitly

proof.text:
By [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] for the residue-ring coefficients, [det-sp-finite-general-ring](3) for general finite $A$, and [det-sp-tower-gamma](2) for towers, $\gamma_f=t_{f,K}(1\otimes a_f)\tau$, with $\tau$ the canonical twist/shift reassociation. Pullback respects this reassociation by the monoidal comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the finite twist comparisons in [det-sp-finite-general-ring]. Substituting the two clauses just proved gives
$$e_Ku^*\gamma_f=t_{f',v^*K}(1\otimes e_1)(1\otimes u^*a_f)\tau'=t_{f',v^*K}(1\otimes a_{f'})\tau'=\gamma_{f'}(v^*K).$$
At tower coefficients all maps in this equality were constructed in the same ordinary derived category; it is an equality there and hence in its full constructible finite-Tor subcategory.

source.place: Last assertion: compose orientation, tensor map, and twist reassociation

split_report.summary: Expanded the implicit setting and made both factor identities explicit. The finite orientation argument uses the actual diagonal, smooth-section deformation and vector-bundle integration; the general finite-ring case uses the mixed coefficient/exchange square. Tower orientation equality is tested only after the single-complex embedding, and tensor coherence is proved in the ringed inverse-system topos by a compactification calculation and an explicit counit computation. No new nodes. Final self-review also supplies finite etale-origin witnesses from the existing Noetherian finite-Tor comparison, checks the witness domains of exchange pasting and tower projection/base change, and writes the diagonal exchange-pasting equation explicitly. Q149 resumed the existing copy, checked all 53 step citations against the current statements and the main-20261015 source, retained the mathematical argument, and supplied the missing direct-delivery report and citation manifest. Maintainer review (Q149): the general compatibility of the compact-support projection map with base change, formerly proved inline in step 5, is now the statement-only node lem-sp-compact-projection-base-change, which step 5 cites; proof_deps and tool_uses were reduced accordingly.
